newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka police recover over 200 illegal guns.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka police recover over 200 illegal guns.

text.p: Sri Lankan police have recovered more than illegal 220 guns since an amnesty to surrender unlicensed firearms ended last month, a newspaper said on Thursday, quoting police officials.
The state-owned Observer said the operation was suspended ahead of last month's local government elections, but was resumed later, netting 228 different kinds of guns from across the island.
Deputy Inspector-General of the police crime branch, Mohammed Nizam, told Reuters last month that 1,500 illegal weapons were handed in to police during the amnesty that ended on March 15.
The government is formulating new laws under the country's emergency regulations to crack down on users, mostly politicians and political activists, of illegal firearms.

The new laws, expected to be finalised this month, provide for a minimum seven-year prison sentence and a maximum sentence of 20 years for the possession of unlicensed guns and other firearms and confiscation of the vehicle or house where illegal firearms are found.

Politicians and political activists in Sri Lanka carry guns, many of them unlicensed, to guard against attacks by separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels, who are fighting for independence in the island's north and east.

But their guns became a key public issue when a young legislator from Sri Lanka's ruling coalition was gunned down in February. An opposition party member was among the suspects detained by police over the killing.
